collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ROLE MODELS AND GOOD EXAMPLES, RM-41 to RM-90 (draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Fifty more events continuing your "Role Models and Good Examples — 40 Events". Same shape as yours: a SETUP, choices A-D (a few have three), and two possible outcomes per choice; the game picks one outcome from the chosen choice.

ledger.before: A villager walking past an empty hut sees
ledger.after: (Name1), walking past an empty hut, sees
ledger.why: the owner (2026-11-15): the person the event is about is a cast villager shown by name, the role word kept as flavor (the villager need not have that job)

collection.description: A villager walking past an empty hut sees a cooking fire still smoldering with no one around and dry leaves blowing nearby.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (Name1), walking past an empty hut, sees a cooking fire still smoldering with no one around and dry leaves blowing nearby.

choices.label: Sweep the Dry Leaves Away and Wait.
Find the Owner and Tell Them.
Suggest Fire Stones Around Every Cooking Pit.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: The villager smothers the embers, and the owner thanks them on returning.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: The owner had banked the fire on purpose to keep it alive and explains, and they agree on a safer way to do it.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: The owner returns shortly, and nothing is lost.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: The wait takes all afternoon, and the villager finds the owner had gone fishing.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: The owner rushes back and banks the fire properly.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: The owner cannot be found, so the villager returns and smothers the embers.

d1.name: Outcome D1
d1.text: Several households add a ring of stones the following week.

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: Some households think the idea fussy, but a few adopt it.
